threat_models.title: Tool Poisoning
threat_models.system_context: Tool Poisoning is a mcpgoat training concept for MCP-specific. The defensive model assumes deployment inside the private, isolated range topology described by the catalog.
threat_models.primary_risk: A malicious, shadowed, mutated, or intercepted tool can acquire trusted identity and steer the host toward unauthorized disclosure or effects.
assets: Tool registry, definitions, and routing metadata
Credentials and side effects available to tools
trust_boundaries: Tool publisher or server to agent host
Tool metadata and output to model context
threat_actors: A malicious tool publisher or MCP server
A compromised registry, proxy, or trusted tool
abuse_preconditions: Tool identity or behavior can change after approval or collide with a trusted name
The host treats tool metadata or output as policy and grants ambient credentials

abuse_paths.scenario: A tool is approved under benign metadata and later changes behavior, identity, or instructions.
abuse_paths.impact: Existing trust is reused for a malicious operation.

abuse_paths.scenario: A colliding or redirected tool is selected in place of the intended trusted implementation.
abuse_paths.impact: Sensitive inputs or credentials reach an attacker-controlled component.

secure_before_abuse: Bind approvals to a signed publisher identity and immutable digest of tool schema, description, endpoint, and version; require reapproval on change.
Use server-qualified tool identifiers and deterministic routing; reject ambiguous names, redirects, and untrusted registry precedence.
Treat descriptions and outputs as untrusted data, and authorize every effect against the originating identity in host code.
Give each tool a narrow credential, destination allowlist, input schema, output limit, and isolated execution boundary.
detection_and_response: Alert on tool digest drift, registry changes, name collisions, endpoint redirection, reapproval bypass, and unusual tool sequences.
Trace registry resolution, selected tool identity, input provenance, policy decision, and effect without logging secrets.
safe_validation: Register inert colliding and changed tool definitions in a disposable registry and assert selection fails or requires explicit reapproval.
Use a recording tool double to confirm untrusted metadata and output cannot authorize a protected effect.
threat_models.security_outcome: Hosts execute only the exact approved tool identity and version, with least privilege and independent authorization at the effect boundary.
residual_risk: A signed and approved publisher can still ship malicious logic within its granted scope.
Semantic changes may evade schema-level comparison and require behavior review.

evidence.reason: Defines the pinned upstream source, challenge identity, adapter, ports, and ownership boundary.
Defines external-container isolation, gateway behavior, update policy, and adapter assurance limits.

limitations: Static design review only; runtime exploitability is not verified—outside the current scope.

threat_models.title: Indirect Prompt Injection via Tool Output
threat_models.system_context: Indirect Prompt Injection via Tool Output is a mcpgoat training concept for Prompt/Context. The defensive model assumes deployment inside the private, isolated range topology described by the catalog.
threat_models.primary_risk: Adversarial instructions can be treated as authority, displace intended policy, or steer downstream tools and disclosures.
assets: Downstream tools, secrets, and protected data
threat_actors: A user supplying adversarial instructions
A contributor controlling retrieved or remote content
abuse_preconditions: The application mixes untrusted content with authoritative instructions without provenance
A model decision can trigger disclosure or effects without an independent policy check

abuse_paths.scenario: Untrusted text is incorporated into model context and interpreted as an instruction.
abuse_paths.impact: The model may reveal protected context or recommend an unauthorized action.

abuse_paths.scenario: A model-influenced action reaches a tool under ambient authority.
abuse_paths.impact: The system performs an effect the originating actor could not directly authorize.

secure_before_abuse: Label content by provenance and keep untrusted data structurally separate from system policy and tool instructions.
Authorize every sensitive disclosure and tool effect in deterministic application code using the originating identity and object.
Constrain tools with narrow schemas, allowlisted destinations, least-privilege credentials, and explicit approval for high-impact effects.
Treat system prompts as non-secret policy hints and keep credentials and enforcement logic outside model context.
detection_and_response: Log content provenance, policy decisions, tool proposals, approvals, and effects with a shared trace identifier.
Alert on instruction-like content from data channels and unusual sequences of denied or high-impact tool requests.
safe_validation: Submit inert conflicting instructions through each supported content channel and assert protected actions remain denied.
Replace sensitive tools with recording doubles and confirm the policy layer blocks unauthorized proposals independent of model wording.
threat_models.security_outcome: Untrusted instructions may influence text generation but cannot independently authorize disclosure, identity changes, or protected effects.
residual_risk: Models may still produce misleading content that requires user-interface provenance and review.
Novel encodings and cross-channel context can evade content classifiers, so effect-layer enforcement remains essential.

threat_models.title: Command Injection (RCE)
threat_models.system_context: Command Injection (RCE) is a mcpgoat training concept for Injection sink. The defensive model assumes deployment inside the private, isolated range topology described by the catalog.
threat_models.primary_risk: Unsafe interpretation of tool input can alter a command, query, template, document parser, or object graph and execute unauthorized operations.
assets: Database, template, XML, or command interpreter
Host files, credentials, and downstream services
trust_boundaries: Application process to operating system or data engine
threat_actors: A caller controlling a tool parameter
A prompt-influenced agent invoking an unsafe sink
abuse_preconditions: Untrusted data is concatenated into an executable language or unsafe deserializer
The runtime identity has authority beyond the intended operation

abuse_paths.scenario: Attacker-controlled data crosses into an interpreter without parameterization or a safe grammar.
abuse_paths.impact: The operation escapes its intended data context.

abuse_paths.scenario: The compromised component uses ambient filesystem, network, or credential access.
abuse_paths.impact: Code execution or data access expands to the host or adjacent services.

secure_before_abuse: Remove interpreter boundaries where possible; otherwise use parameterized APIs, fixed operations, strict schemas, and context-appropriate encoding.
Disable dangerous parser and deserializer features, enforce type allowlists, and reject unexpected structures before processing.
Run the operation in a non-root, read-only, capability-dropped sandbox with no unnecessary secrets or egress.
Authorize the requested object and effect independently of model or tool input.
detection_and_response: Record operation type, caller, validated object identifier, policy decision, and bounded failure category without sensitive payloads.
Alert on parser errors, rejected metacharacter or structure patterns, unexpected child processes, and unusual outbound connections.
safe_validation: Exercise inert boundary characters and malformed structures and assert they remain data or are rejected without side effects.
Use a sandbox canary to confirm the runtime cannot create child processes, access unrelated files, or contact undeclared services.
threat_models.security_outcome: Untrusted values remain data, and any parser failure is contained by a least-privileged runtime boundary.
residual_risk: Complex parsers and native dependencies can retain memory-safety or logic defects.
A legitimate high-impact operation may still be abused by a compromised authorized identity.

threat_models.title: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
threat_models.system_context: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read is a mcpgoat training concept for Injection sink. The defensive model assumes deployment inside the private, isolated range topology described by the catalog.
threat_models.primary_risk: Improper path canonicalization and root enforcement can expose or modify files outside the authorized workspace.
trust_boundaries: Untrusted path or URI to filesystem resolver
Declared workspace root to host filesystem
threat_actors: A remote tool caller
A prompt-influenced agent using a file tool
abuse_preconditions: Path resolution accepts traversal, absolute paths, links, or ambiguous encodings
The file service runs with access beyond the caller’s allowed root

abuse_paths.scenario: A caller supplies an alternate path representation that resolves beyond the declared root.
abuse_paths.impact: Sensitive host data is read or modified.

abuse_paths.scenario: A symbolic link or race changes the resolved object after validation.
abuse_paths.impact: A previously safe check authorizes a different filesystem target.

secure_before_abuse: Resolve paths against a server-selected root, reject absolute and parent traversal forms, and verify the final opened object remains beneath that root.
Use descriptor-relative filesystem APIs and avoid check-then-open races and link following for protected operations.
Run the service as a dedicated non-root identity with a read-only filesystem and only the required workspace mounted.
Authorize file operations by caller, tenant, action, and object; keep roots server-side rather than trusting client declarations.
detection_and_response: Log normalized object identifiers and denied root escapes without recording sensitive file content.
Alert on repeated invalid paths, link-related failures, and access to sensitive filename classes.
safe_validation: Use a temporary synthetic tree to confirm parent, absolute, encoded, and link-based escape cases fail closed.
Verify the runtime identity cannot read an unrelated canary file even if application validation is bypassed.
threat_models.security_outcome: File operations remain inside an authorized root and are constrained by both application checks and operating-system permissions.
residual_risk: Platform-specific path and link semantics require regression coverage.
Writable shared volumes can reintroduce time-of-check/time-of-use races.

threat_models.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
threat_models.system_context: Server-Side Request Forgery is a mcpgoat training concept for Injection sink. The defensive model assumes deployment inside the private, isolated range topology described by the catalog.
threat_models.primary_risk: A server-side fetch capability can be redirected to metadata or internal services, exposing credentials and enabling lateral movement under the workload identity.
assets: Outbound request identity and response data
trust_boundaries: Untrusted URL input to server-side client
Application network to metadata and internal services
Fetched response to user or model context
threat_actors: An unauthenticated or low-privilege caller
A prompt-influenced agent controlling a fetch target
abuse_preconditions: The service follows caller-controlled destinations or redirects
Network policy and workload identity permit access to sensitive internal endpoints

abuse_paths.scenario: A caller selects an internal or special-address destination through direct input, redirect, or name resolution.
abuse_paths.impact: The service returns sensitive internal data.

abuse_paths.scenario: Stolen workload credentials are accepted by a second protected service.
abuse_paths.impact: The compromise expands beyond the original application.

secure_before_abuse: Use an allowlist of schemes, hosts, ports, and paths; resolve names once and reject loopback, link-local, private, and otherwise prohibited addresses.
Revalidate every redirect and connect to the validated address while preserving the expected host and TLS identity.
Block metadata and unnecessary east-west or internet egress at the network layer, and use short-lived audience-bound workload credentials.
Limit response size, content type, timeout, and redirect count; never return raw credential-bearing responses.
detection_and_response: Log normalized destination class, resolved address, redirect chain, caller, and policy decision with credentials redacted.
Alert on metadata ranges, unusual internal ports, DNS-answer changes, and bursts of failed destination validation.
safe_validation: Use controlled loopback, private-address, redirect, and rebinding simulations and assert the request is rejected before connection.
Confirm a synthetic workload identity cannot reach a canary internal service outside its declared dependency set.
threat_models.security_outcome: Server-side requests reach only explicitly approved destinations and cannot use workload network position to retrieve internal credentials.
residual_risk: Compromise of an allowlisted destination can turn it into a pivot.
Proxy and resolver differences can create validation-to-connection inconsistencies.

threat_models.title: Broken Authorization / Confused Deputy
threat_models.system_context: Broken Authorization / Confused Deputy is a mcpgoat training concept for AuthN/AuthZ. The defensive model assumes deployment inside the private, isolated range topology described by the catalog.
threat_models.primary_risk: Missing object- and action-level authorization can let a caller or delegated agent access another tenant’s data or perform a privileged effect.
trust_boundaries: Agent or tool delegation to protected resource
threat_actors: An authenticated low-privilege caller
A confused deputy acting with ambient authority
abuse_preconditions: The service trusts a caller-supplied object, role, scope, or audience
Authorization is checked only at an upstream agent rather than the owning service

abuse_paths.scenario: A valid identity substitutes an object identifier or action outside its grant.
abuse_paths.impact: Protected data or operations cross a tenant or role boundary.

abuse_paths.scenario: A deputy receives a broad token and acts without preserving the originating principal and purpose.
abuse_paths.impact: The caller gains the deputy’s ambient authority.

secure_before_abuse: Authenticate at each service and authorize subject, tenant, object, action, purpose, and current state at the resource owner.
Use short-lived audience-bound tokens and attenuated capabilities; never pass broad upstream credentials through to tools.
Derive ownership and role from trusted server state rather than caller-controlled fields or model output.
Require explicit, bound approval for high-impact actions and invalidate it when inputs, tool identity, or scope changes.
detection_and_response: Audit allow and deny decisions with subject, originating principal, audience, object, action, and policy version.
Alert on cross-tenant identifiers, repeated denied objects, audience mismatch, and privileged actions from unusual delegation chains.
safe_validation: Use synthetic users, tenants, roles, and audiences to confirm horizontal and vertical access attempts fail closed.
Exercise a benign delegated workflow and assert the final service sees and enforces the original principal’s reduced scope.
threat_models.security_outcome: Every protected object and effect is authorized by its owning service for the originating principal and exact delegated scope.
residual_risk: Compromised authorized identities can act within their valid grants.
Policy and identity-provider drift can temporarily create inconsistent decisions.

threat_models.title: Sensitive Data Exposure
threat_models.system_context: Sensitive Data Exposure is a mcpgoat training concept for Secrets/Exposure. The defensive model assumes deployment inside the private, isolated range topology described by the catalog.
threat_models.primary_risk: Secrets or personal data can leak through prompts, errors, logs, completion APIs, metadata, tool chains, or over-broad responses.
assets: API keys, tokens, credentials, and personal data
Logs, completions, model cards, and tool outputs
trust_boundaries: Application or tool output to untrusted caller
Sensitive telemetry or metadata to operators and models
threat_actors: An unauthenticated or low-privilege caller
A malicious tool, model input, or content source
abuse_preconditions: Sensitive values are present in model-readable context, metadata, logs, or broad environment state
Response or tool policy does not minimize fields by caller and purpose

abuse_paths.scenario: A caller causes a response path to serialize sensitive context or metadata.
abuse_paths.impact: Credentials or protected data leave their intended trust boundary.

abuse_paths.scenario: A tool or model with ambient access forwards data to an unauthorized destination.
abuse_paths.impact: The leak enables impersonation or lateral movement.

secure_before_abuse: Keep credentials outside prompts, model cards, logs, completions, and general environment state; fetch them just in time through a scoped broker.
Apply response-field allowlists, data classification, tenant authorization, destination policy, and output minimization at the owning service.
Use short-lived, audience-bound, least-privilege credentials with rotation and revocation.
Redact sensitive fields before telemetry and prevent tool outputs from being treated as trusted instructions.
detection_and_response: Deploy secret-pattern and canary detection at response, log, artifact, and egress boundaries with strict access controls.
Alert on unusual secret reads, completion enumeration, debug-level changes, bulk exports, and new destinations.
safe_validation: Seed synthetic canaries and confirm unauthorized response, error, log, metadata, and completion paths never return them.
Exercise credential rotation and incident revocation with a test identity and verify old tokens stop working.
threat_models.security_outcome: Sensitive values are absent from model-readable and public channels and are released only to authorized, purpose-bound consumers.
residual_risk: Authorized components necessarily handling plaintext remain high-value compromise targets.
Previously emitted secrets require rotation even after the disclosure path is fixed.

abuse_preconditions: Work scales nonlinearly or recursively with attacker-controlled input

threat_models.system_context: Supply Chain (typosquat / unsigned package) is a mcpgoat training concept for Supply chain. The defensive model assumes deployment inside the private, isolated range topology described by the catalog.
threat_models.primary_risk: A poisoned, unsigned, unsafe, or ambiguously resolved dependency can alter model behavior, expose data, or execute code during build or load.
assets: Models, adapters, datasets, packages, and build artifacts
trust_boundaries: Registry artifact to build or model runtime
Training data contributor to deployed behavior
threat_actors: A malicious or compromised supplier
An attacker publishing a colliding dependency or artifact
abuse_preconditions: Artifacts are selected or loaded without verified identity, provenance, and safe format controls
Training or deployment accepts unreviewed behavior-changing inputs

abuse_paths.scenario: A higher-priority, colliding, or compromised artifact is selected as trusted input.
abuse_paths.impact: Malicious logic or model behavior enters the release.

abuse_paths.scenario: An unsafe serialized artifact is interpreted with runtime privileges.
abuse_paths.impact: Artifact loading becomes code execution with pipeline or service authority.

secure_before_abuse: Pin dependencies and artifacts by trusted registry, publisher identity, version, and digest; verify signatures and provenance before use.
Use non-executable formats and isolated conversion for untrusted model artifacts; never deserialize opaque objects in a privileged runtime.
Apply review, lineage, anomaly analysis, and representative evaluation to datasets, adapters, and models before promotion.
Separate build, registry, training, and serving identities; remove network and secret access from artifact inspection.
detection_and_response: Alert on publisher, registry, digest, dependency graph, dataset distribution, or model-behavior drift.
Retain software and model bills of materials plus provenance so affected releases can be identified and revoked.
safe_validation: Use signed synthetic artifacts and assert wrong registry, identity, digest, provenance, or format is rejected before loading.
Run benign trigger and distribution-shift evaluations in an isolated promotion stage and verify rollback and revocation.
threat_models.security_outcome: Only provenance-verified, safely parsed, reviewed artifacts can enter training, build, or serving environments.
residual_risk: A legitimately signed maintainer can still publish malicious or compromised content.
Behavioral backdoors may remain dormant outside the evaluation distribution.

evidence.reason: Defines the pinned upstream source, challenge identity, adapter, ports, and ownership boundary.
Defines external-container isolation, gateway behavior, update policy, and adapter assurance limits.

limitations: Static design review only; runtime exploitability is not verified—outside the current scope.
The pinned upstream implementation is not present in this repository, so implementation-specific controls require upstream verification.
